input.question: why does renting a movie digitally cost so much more (usually 4-5 dollars) than renting a physical disc from a service like RedBox (usually 1-2 dollars)?
input.ground_truth: Simply a convenience fee. Also, movie companies charge a lot more for digital rights, as more people will stream/download them than buy the physical copy, that's why Netflix's physical library is much larger than their digital library.

Question: why does renting a movie digitally cost so much more (usually 4-5 dollars) than renting a physical disc from a service like RedBox (usually 1-2 dollars)?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay, let’s imagine you want to borrow a toy from your friend.

If you go to RedBox, it’s like borrowing a toy that your friend keeps in a big box outside. Lots of people can borrow the same toy, and it doesn’t cost your friend very much to let you borrow it for a little while. That’s why it only costs you a dollar or two.

But if you want to watch a movie digitally, it’s like asking your friend to make a brand new copy of their toy just for you. Making a new copy takes more work and costs more money. That’s why it costs more—because the movie company has to make a special copy just for you to watch, and they want to get paid for that extra work.

So, borrowing a real disc is cheaper because lots of people can share it. Watching a movie online is more expensive because it’s like getting your very own copy just for you!
